purpose: Screen whether FreeCAD's native C++ DXF importer preserves a generated tilted planar AC1021 control-point SPLINE through dwg2dxf.

source.provenance: Generated locally from scratch by a temporary extension to tests/dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp; the DWG was kept under the system temporary directory and is not a repository fixture.

dxf.inspection: The SPLINE record retains degree 2, six knots, three group-10 WCS control points exactly as authored, and the calculated group-210 plane normal.

consumer.route: LibreDWG-only dwg2dxf conversion followed by FreeCAD Draft C++ DXF importer
consumer.expectedMaximumYDerivation: For a clamped degree-2 spline with these three poles and knots, y(t)=32+10t(1-t), whose maximum is 34.5 at t=0.5.

result: The DWG-to-DXF converter completed and emitted the authored WCS control-point values, but FreeCAD's imported shape bounds disagreed with the exact quadratic curve. This is a consumer semantic mismatch for this generated profile; it does not establish a libdxfrw parser/writer defect or qualify SPLINE support.

validation.experimentalFreecadOpenInsert: FAIL: both operations imported one SPLINE with no unsupported-feature report, but the imported geometry maximum Y was 35.4375 instead of 34.5.
validation.restoredPrimitiveProfile: PASS: existing POINT/LINE/CIRCLE/ARC/ELLIPSE/LWPOLYLINE open and insert selectors passed 2/2 after removing SPLINE from the profile.
validation.fixturePolicy: No DWG or DXF fixture was committed.

nextAction: Keep tilted SPLINE out of the passing FreeCAD support profile. Resolve the WCS/control-point interpretation with an independent CAD consumer or native producer/consumer witness before deciding whether any libdxfrw change is warranted. Preserve the original six-entity profile meanwhile.
supportClaimEffect: None; this receipt records a failing consumer qualification and does not promote or withdraw a general support claim.
